evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'I just need to ask you some questions about it might take about ten to fifteen minutes if this is a good time?' — time-boxed but no explicit promise of a dependable quote, and rushed past without a clear wait for yes.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Henry Cho), moving day (thirtieth/Wednesday), city-to-city route (2724 Kipling Street to 5103 Pine Reach Drive), and size (one bedroom, 619 sq ft) all covered.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Joanna: 'do you have any important concerns or instructions for this move that you also want us to discuss on this call?' — asked, but only after confirming addresses and property details had already begun.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'No' to concerns; no concerns raised, so N/A.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns raised by customer, so N/A.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment/home), floors (second floor with elevator, two-story destination), rooms (one bedroom), walking distance (30-40 feet from elevator), additional furniture (mattress, desk, couch, small coffee table), parking (driveway, no issues). All seven items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Joanna: 'are you gonna pack everything into boxes or do you need help with that as well?' — customer declined packing help.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Joanna: 'Do you think you would just have around fifteen to 25 boxes or do you think you'll have more?' — asked and answered (15-25 boxes).
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'typically a one bedroom apartment usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours in terms of completion. So that would be an estimated budget of $475.65 to $665' — range given with typical time frame for property size; personalized to one-bedroom profile.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Joanna disclosed hourly rates ($95/mover, $190 for two), mentioned all-inclusive pricing (taxes, insurance, credit card fees, assembly, transportation), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute intervals. No trip fee/overnight fee explicitly mentioned but full framing otherwise present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Joanna moved directly to 'would you like our help with your move on Wednesday?' without asking 'does that feel fair' or pausing for customer reaction to the estimate.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Joanna: 'lastly on time guarantee if we run late we provide discounts for your move' — mentioned, discount terms stated (discounts if late), though could have been more explicit about 'starts discounting immediately.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Joanna: 'we'll also include our no worries damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage' — coverage amount and inclusion stated, but no explicit mention of 'no deductible / no fine print' framing or that it's built into the rate vs. add-on.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No closing of the loop. Joanna did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or confirm whether the two promises resolved the customer's concerns. Instead, she moved directly to the ask.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Joanna: 'Now that being said would you like our help with your move on Wednesday?' — asked plainly without a soft out.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Not confirmed. Customer said 'I'm gonna think about it. And maybe call somewhere else.' Joanna responded with 'We sent this via email...If you're ready to book it, just you know, respond to the email give us a call.' No date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or crew notes confirmed because the booking was not accepted.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details (property type, floor, walking distance, furniture, parking, box count) and provided a fully-anchored, hourly-rate estimate with strong pricing transparency (all-inclusive, no hidden fees, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute intervals).
coaching_note: After delivering the estimate, pause and ask 'Does that feel fair?' with genuine silence to let the customer absorb the pricing — then address the customer's actual objection (2.5-hour minimum concern) before asking for the business, and confirm booking details if they agree.
